Supporting slack has conditional expectation zero on a labeled face, so the output stays on the same plane. The affine moments vanish by source localization and covariance increments annihilate the full facet normal.

At a regular boundary point of a positive actual fiber, at least one active facet is nonvertical, and each such active facet has the unique continuous normal of the fiber there. The first active matching facet gives a Borel source label. The transported target owner density can differ from a deterministic owner selection. The partition preserves the original allocations ζ_j on cut sections.

Fiberwise Gauss–Green has a minus section term from outward cut normal −v_j. At inside support the two terms with the same normal combine with α+σ=1. At outside support opposite terms cancel with α=σ. The same check uses counting measure in dimension one.

Subtracting the cap-volume flux gives a positive section-height integral. Expanding at the common full centroid gives the negative base covariance and leaves the constant S_j times the common base or continuous centroid times b_j−a_j·p̄_i. The supplied λ_jS_j=t_iρ_j and centered height balance cancel those constants. The continuous moment calculation uses div[x(h·x)]=(d+1)h·x, so the section centroid must include x. The full facet and section kernels convert −(Q_f^{px})ᵀa_f and −(V_j^{px})ᵀa_j into their claimed positive continuous-block forms.

Recomputed the two rational flux signs on actual interval fibers [−1/2,1/2] at p=−1,0,1 with caps x+p/4≥0 and −x≥0, weights one, and identity boundary coupling. The base and continuous residuals are −1/2 and 1/8. The section covariance contributions give those same two numbers. overlap.comparison: The marked martingale equivalence supplies a coupling under localized convex-order assumptions. This result starts from a given coupling and resolves its labeled variance and allocated section flux.
The actual-fiber theorem proves normal preservation and exposed-face support for physical martingales. It does not split target owner fractions or give the grouped mixed-flux identities.

The shared-plane separator supplies its own affine face stresses and common section centroids. This result computes covariances of a given physical transport and uses its induced target fractions instead.
The allocation branch identity agrees. The present proof needs its independent transport variance and covariance expansion after subtracting the cap flux.

Its limiting group theorem establishes a common full mean and normal balance under separate contact and convergence hypotheses. It does not supply the mixed-flux covariance conclusion for these supplied data.

readability: The grouping is read as a partition of the positive-section caps, as required by the definition of every V_j and the grouped cancellation. Stating this directly would make the quantifier easier to parse.
review_method: Independent cold proof read, source and accepted-fact comparison, and exact rational recalculation.
summary: The localized variance and facet kernel are correct under the given marked martingale. Both mixed-flux identities hold for the original section allocations with the grouped full centroid and height balance.
